question: Which one of the following classical dances in its present form is influenced by Mughal tradition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• This dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• During the Mughal era, Kathak evolved to include intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures influenced by Persian and Mughal cultures.
 
• The dance is characterized by its intricate footwork and spins, which are performed to the accompaniment of classical Hindustani music.
 
• Kathak dancers traditionally wear elaborate costumes that are reflective of Mughal influences, including heavy jewelry and embroidered dresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from Kerala, known for its graceful movements and feminine style.
 
• **Kathakali** is another classical dance from Kerala, noted for its elaborate costumes and dramatic storytelling.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a classical dance from Tamil Nadu, characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork.
 
• While these other dance forms have their own unique histories and styles, it is Kathak that prominently reflects the influence of Mughal tradition.
